text.p: Compuserve Inc expects to be profitable again in 1996/97 despite losses in the first and second quarters, said Steven Stanbrook, president of international operations.

Stanbrook told a news conference here the U.S.-based online service, the world's second largest, would turn profits in the third and fourth quarters of the year ending April 30, 1997 that would more than make up for the losses in the first half.
"This year will be no exception in the 27-year history of Compuserve. We have never had a loss for a full year," Stanbrook said.
Compuserve's worldwide subscriber base could grow to six million by the end of the fiscal year from five million in April 1996, he said.
The company lost 32 cents a share in the first quarter and expects to lose up to 15 cents a share in the current quarter.
Stanbrook attributed the first and second quarter losses to high investments, particularly in the U.S., adding the company is already turning good profits in Europe.
German unit Compuserve GmbH announced an agreement allowing its users cheaper access via Deutsche Telekom AG's network.
"The German market is of great strategic importance to us," Stanbrook said. Compuserve's German subscriber base could rise to 400,000 next April from 290,000 now, he said.
The service hopes for a boost from the lower rates, which will let Compuserve users throughout Germany dial in using "City" rates instead of long-distance.
They will also be able to access Compuserve via Telekom's Datex-J nodes for an access fee of $1 per hour, down from $14.20 per hour.
